raw_response:
Aiya, let me sit down and think about this year. My husband and I have been doing the same thing for so many years, but I'll walk through it like my daughter-in-law asked me to.

**Land.** I've got 11.6 mu altogether. The big piece near the canal, about 9 mu, is my wheat-maize ground — always has been. The patch by the village road, around 2 and a half mu, that's my cotton land, been growing cotton on it since before my second boy was born. And I keep a little corner, maybe 1 mu behind the maize plot, for mungbean — the old folks always grew mungbean for the family, you boil it in summer for the heat, and I save seed every year. I won't change what goes where. Changing is how you lose money.

**Wheat (9 mu).** I'll sow around Shuang Jiang (霜降), end of October, same as always. I saved seed from last year's harvest — why pay for seed? My husband says the bought seed grows bigger but I don't trust spending that money. Before plowing I put down about one bag of 二铵 (the black-and-white bag, compound fertilizer) for every 2 and a half mu or so — that's 3 bags, maybe a bit more. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, if it looks yellow I put down urea, about one bag per 2 mu, so 4 or 5 bags. Water it in winter once to settle the ground, then again at green-up, and one more time at jointing if there's no rain. That's three waterings usually. If the weeds are bad I buy that herbicide from the agricultural shop, the cheap one. No bugs usually on wheat, I don't spray. The combine man comes in June and takes his share in grain or I pay him cash. Last year I got about 350 jin per mu (175 kg), not bad. Hoping for similar.

Wait — I'm saying jin, let me think in kg like my son tells me. That's about 350 kg per mu. Yes.

**Maize (8 mu).** Right after wheat comes off in mid-June, no time to waste — my husband hires the planter man with the tractor and he sows it the next day. Seed I buy, can't save maize seed, it doesn't come true — the shop owner says "Zhengdan" or "Xianyu", I take whatever the neighbors say worked last year. About 50 yuan per mu for seed. I put down one bag of compound per 2 mu at planting time, then one bag of urea per 2 mu when the maize is waist-high. Water once in July if the sky is dry. Spray herbicide after planting, one time, that's enough. The stalks give fodder for the neighbor's goats, he gives me a bit back. Combine comes in late September. Get about 400-450 kg per mu if the rain is right.

**Mungbean (1 mu).** I sow it end of June, broadcast by hand, I don't even till properly — just scratch the ground with the hoe. Seed I saved, free. No fertilizer, mungbean doesn't need it, my mother always said mungbean feeds itself. No water either, it's tough. I pick the pods when they turn black, takes three or four times through the field in August. Maybe 80 kg for the whole patch. Most of it we eat, a little I sell in the market when I go.

**Cotton (2.6 mu).** This one is hardest — lots of work, my back aches from picking. I sow around Gu Yu (谷雨), end of April, after soaking the seed overnight. Cheap seed, the Bt kind, about 40 yuan per mu. One bag of compound before planting for the whole patch, then one bag of urea at squaring time. Water once in July and once in August if the well has water — the electric pump bill is big so I don't water more than needed. Spray for bugs maybe three times — the aphids and the bollworm, even with Bt seed you still get some. I pick by hand through September, October, even into November — my husband helps on weekends, my daughter-in-law helps when she's free. Get about 220-240 kg of lint per mu, and the price has been so-so.

**Money and labor.** I figure I can spend maybe 7,000 yuan on inputs this year — that's what we've set aside from last year's sales and my older son's wage money. If fertilizer goes up again I'll use less urea on maize, the wheat comes first. For labor, it's me, my husband, and my daughter-in-law when she's home from her factory job. The children are away. I hire the planter, the combine, that's it. Everything else we do ourselves.
